note: Every item has low / typ / high and a source id. Sources marked estimate have no published figure behind them; basis says how the number was reached. Dollar figures are as published, not adjusted for inflation unless the basis says so.

ag_valuation_share.label: Ag valuation share of market value

fence_upkeep_pct.label: Fence repair
fence_upkeep_pct.unit: share of fence cost per year

equipment_upkeep_pct.label: Equipment fuel and repairs
equipment_upkeep_pct.unit: share of equipment cost per year

household_spending_rural.label: Household spending less housing and healthcare

egg_dozen_value.label: Store value of a dozen eggs

lease_apc.label: Acres per cow on leased grass

calf_income_share.label: Share of a cow's yearly income that is calves, not culls

cow_share_operator.label: Operator share of calf money on leased cows

pair_rent_month.label: Pasture rent per pair per month

stocker_grazing_budget.label: Grazing cost built into the stocker budget

stocker_acres.label: Acres per stocker for the season

beef_hanging_price.label: Beef sold by the half or quarter

calf_weaned_value.label: Weaned steer calf at the sale barn

finish_carry.label: Carrying a calf a year to finish, not counting grass

rent_monthly.label: Rent for a house in the country

ngwa_2021.name: National Ground Water Association, Well Owners Guide
ngwa_2021.basis: Drilling ran about $24 a foot for a 4-inch well and $30 for a 6-inch well, casing extra. A household submersible pump ran $3,000 to $3,200. The high figure here adds casing and five years of price rises.

umn_well_2022.name: University of Minnesota Extension, Digging or expanding a well
umn_well_2022.basis: A new well for a 5 to 20 acre farm: $5,000 to $30,000.

usgs_well_depth_2021.name: USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2021-5069, depth of groundwater used for drinking water
usgs_well_depth_2021.basis: Median depth of US domestic wells is 142 ft; public supply wells 202 ft.

epa_septic_2018.name: US EPA Water Finance Clearinghouse, Financing Septic Systems
epa_septic_2018.basis: Conventional system installed, with permits: $3,000 to $15,000. Alternative and advanced systems: $10,000 to $30,000. State examples ran $4,000 to $18,000.

mu_septic_2017.name: University of Missouri Extension EQM104F, Household Wastewater
mu_septic_2017.basis: Pumping a tank: $100 to $250, every 3 to 5 years. High figure allows for an aerobic service contract.

coop_line_ext.name: Rural electric co-op line extension policies: Webster Electric (MO) 2025, Upper Cumberland EMC (TN) 2025, Cullman Electric (AL) 2023, Missouri PSC comparison 2015
coop_line_ext.basis: Webster: first 200 ft free, then $5 a foot overhead. Cullman: first 400 ft free, then $13 overhead, $20 underground. UCEMC: $17 a foot overhead. Missouri PSC survey: $15 overhead, $23 underground. Texas and Oklahoma co-ops publish a free allowance ($1,950 to $7,500) and charge the rest at cost.

eia_bill_2024.name: US EIA, Table 5.A, 2024 average monthly residential electric bill by state
eia_bill_2024.basis: US $142 a month. Missouri $129, Arkansas $129, Oklahoma $132, Kentucky $134, Tennessee $143, Texas $164, Alabama $174.

nrel_solar_2025.name: US DOE SETO and NREL, Solar Photovoltaic System Cost Benchmarks, Q1 2025
nrel_solar_2025.basis: An 8 kW home system with a 13.5 kWh battery: $4.33 to $4.59 a watt installed, about $35,000 to $37,000. Off-grid needs more battery.

energysage_offgrid_2026.name: EnergySage, Off-Grid Solar: Costs, Process, and Best Products, and Solar Battery Cost
energysage_offgrid_2026.basis: A full off-grid system for an average house often runs $115,000 or more. A 13.5 kWh battery runs about $15,600 installed. Low here is the NREL 8 kW system with one battery ($35,000); typical adds two more batteries, sized for a modest house that uses less than average.

isu_fence_2024.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker B1-75, Estimated Costs for Livestock Fencing
isu_fence_2024.basis: Per foot built, labor at $20 an hour, no gates: woven wire $2.34, 5-strand barbed $1.99, high-tensile electric $1.21.

mu_fence_2026.name: University of Missouri Extension G1193, Pasture Fence Construction Budget
mu_fence_2026.basis: Per foot built, with a gate: woven wire $3.94, 5-strand barbed $3.03, electric high-tensile $2.51. Low here is the Iowa State 2024 figure for the same fence; typical is the middle of the two.

pole_barn_prices.name: Morton Buildings (2022) and FBi Buildings (2021) published shell pricing; Hansen Pole Buildings kit prices (2026)
pole_barn_prices.basis: Erected shell $25 to $55 a square foot depending on size; kit materials only $9 to $13; concrete and finish add $50 or more. Typical here is a 30 x 40 erected shell with a slab.

nahb_2024.name: NAHB, Cost of Constructing a Home 2024
nahb_2024.basis: Average construction cost $428,215 for 2,647 sq ft, about $162 a square foot, not counting the lot. Low and high here spread 20% either side.

fbi_barndo_2024.name: FBi Buildings, How Much Does a 1,500 Square Foot Barndominium Cost
fbi_barndo_2024.basis: Shell $45 to $75 a square foot; finished $125 basic, $150 to $400 with upgrades.

census_mhs_2025.name: US Census Bureau, Manufactured Housing Survey, average sales price of new manufactured homes, 2025
census_mhs_2025.basis: Single-section $85,600, double-section $157,100, all homes $127,200. Factory price, before delivery and setup.

closingcorp_2021.name: CoreLogic ClosingCorp, Purchase Mortgage Closing Cost Report 2021
closingcorp_2021.basis: Closing costs averaged 1.01% of price without transfer taxes and 1.81% with. Cash land deals skip lender fees; land loans add origination.

survey_cost.name: University of Missouri Extension G5055 (2017, reviewed 2026) and LandThink, Tips on Rural Land Surveys (2019)
survey_cost.basis: $2,500 for a boundary survey on a 100-acre example; $3,000 to $6,000 for an 80-acre tract.

naic_home_2023.name: NAIC, Homeowners Insurance Report, data for 2023, Table 4
naic_home_2023.basis: Average owner-occupied home premium: US $1,731, Texas $2,762, Oklahoma $2,398, Arkansas $1,868, Missouri $1,675, Tennessee $1,644, Kentucky $1,484. A farm or ranch policy adds barns, fence, equipment and liability; no published average for that, so the typical and high here are an estimate above the home figure.

tamu_cowcalf_2025.name: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension, 2025 cow-calf budgets, North Texas District 4, improved and native pasture
tamu_cowcalf_2025.basis: Cash costs per cow with your own labor taken out: about $330 on improved pasture, $510 on native pasture (hay $159 to $318, marketing $40, mineral $19, vet $25, supplement, fuel, repairs, interest). High is the USDA ERS 2024 US operating cost of $690.

ers_cowcalf_2025.name: USDA ERS, Commodity Costs and Returns, cow-calf, US total, dollars per cow
ers_cowcalf_2025.basis: Operating costs per cow: $716 (2023), $690 (2024), $676 (2025). Gross value of production per cow, calves and culls: $925 (2023), $1,120 (2024), $1,417 (2025).

isu_livestock_2026.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker B1-21, Livestock Enterprise Budgets for Iowa 2026
isu_livestock_2026.basis: Figures a beef cow at $2,300, a bull at $5,000 over 25 cows, a utility tractor at $30,000, 2.1 tons of hay per cow per year, 0.9 calf weaned per cow.

tpwd_stocking.name: Texas Parks and Wildlife, Post Oak Savannah and Blackland Prairie habitat management, livestock
tpwd_stocking.basis: One cow with calf per 3 to 6 acres on bermuda or bahia pasture, 8 to 15 acres on native grass. Texas A&M budgets figure 2.1 to 3.1 acres on North Texas improved and native pasture.

ams_cattle_2026.name: USDA AMS, Texas Weekly Cattle Auction Summary, week of November 8 to 14, 2026, and Oklahoma National Stockyards, November 10, 2026
ams_cattle_2026.basis: Bred cows, medium and large frame, 5 to 8 years old: $1,882 to $2,570 average in Texas, $3,058 in Oklahoma City. Younger bred cows $2,809. Pairs $3,250. One week of sales, not a yearly average.

bull_sales_2025.name: UGA Calhoun Bull Evaluation Sale summary (December 2025) and Iowa State 2026 budget assumption
bull_sales_2025.basis: 71 tested bulls averaged $7,634, high $14,000. Iowa State budgets figure a bull at $5,000.

mu_goat_2027.name: University of Missouri Extension G691 and G690, Meat Goat Planning Budgets, 2027 and 2024
mu_goat_2027.basis: Replacement doe $326 (2027 budget) and $210 (2024 budget); buck $651 and $270. Operating cost per doe $222 (2024) to $398 (2027, with $106 of labor). Income per doe $381 (2027). About one doe per acre.

ext_horses.name: Extension Horses (horses.extension.org), Cost of Horse Ownership and The Real Cost of Owning a Horse
ext_horses.basis: Feed and operating about $2,427 a year per horse; feeding $100 to $250 a month, farrier $25 to $50 every 6 to 8 weeks, vaccines $75 to $125 twice a year, dewormer $50. Older prices; the high here allows for that.

umd_layers_2026.name: University of Maryland and University of Delaware Extension, FS-2025-0783, Backyard Layer Flock Economics
umd_layers_2026.basis: 10 birds over 3 years: $1,759 all in, 522 dozen eggs, $3.37 a dozen. Simple coop and run $500; feeder, waterer, storage and heater $225. Chicks $6. Running cost works out to about $36 a bird a year and 17 dozen eggs a bird.

ncsu_garden_2017.name: NC State Extension AG-806, Community Food Gardening Handbook, funding section
ncsu_garden_2017.basis: Start-up for a basic quarter-acre garden: roughly $1,000 to $5,000, fence and water the biggest costs.

joe_garden_2014.name: Journal of Extension 52(2), Langellotto, Economic Costs and Benefits of Home Vegetable Gardens
joe_garden_2014.basis: Home gardens produced about $677 of food beyond $238 of supplies, so about $915 of food a year at 2014 prices. The typical and high here allow for price rises since.

uky_apple_2020.name: University of Kentucky Center for Crop Diversification, Apple Economics
uky_apple_2020.basis: Establishing an orchard: $7,225 an acre for 155 semi-dwarf trees, about $47 a tree with prep and irrigation; $23 a tree at 340 trees an acre. A few trees bought retail cost more each.

utv_2024.name: DTN Progressive Farmer, Polaris 2025 Ranger line pricing

bls_ces_2025.name: BLS, Consumer Expenditures 2025
bls_ces_2025.basis: Average household spent $81,905 in 2025: housing $27,790, transportation $13,492, food $10,633, healthcare $6,470. Spending out there is figured as the total less housing and healthcare, which the calculator counts on their own lines.

kff_premiums_2025.name: KFF, 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey, and Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums
kff_premiums_2025.basis: Employer family coverage averaged $26,993 a year, about $2,250 a month, which is roughly what COBRA costs when you leave. Marketplace benchmark plan for one 40-year-old: $625 a month in 2026, before any subsidy.

est_land_spread.name: Estimate: price spread
est_land_spread.basis: Low is 15% under your price, high 20% over. Land is what the seller takes.

est_mobile_used.name: Estimate: used mobile home price
est_mobile_used.basis: No published average for used manufactured homes exists (Census tracks new homes only; new single-section averaged $85,600 in 2025). Clean used single-wides commonly change hands for a quarter to half of that; double-wides more.

est_mobile_setup.name: Estimate: delivery and setup of a manufactured home
est_mobile_setup.basis: Transport, pad or piers, tie-downs, skirting, steps, utility hookups. No published average; figures are what movers and installers commonly quote.

est_well_pump.name: Estimate: pump package
est_well_pump.basis: NGWA puts a household submersible pump at $3,000 to $3,200 (2021). Pressure tank, wiring, trench and line to the house are added as an estimate.

est_well_annual.name: Estimate: well upkeep
est_well_annual.basis: Pump power plus a fund to replace a $3,000 pump every 10 to 15 years.

est_electric_service.name: Estimate: meter pole and hookup
est_electric_service.basis: Meter pole, meter loop and a 200-amp panel set by an electrician. Co-ops often cover the transformer within their free allowance.

est_solar_annual.name: Estimate: solar upkeep
est_solar_annual.basis: A battery fund (a $15,600 battery lasts 10 to 15 years) plus cleaning and an inverter fund.

est_fence_upkeep.name: Estimate: fence repair
est_fence_upkeep.basis: 1% to 4% of what the fence cost, each year, for staples, posts, wire and a stretcher day.

est_equip_upkeep.name: Estimate: equipment fuel and repairs
est_equip_upkeep.basis: 5% to 12% of what the equipment cost, each year, for fuel, oil, tires, batteries and repairs.

est_tractor.name: Estimate: used tractor
est_tractor.basis: Iowa State 2026 budgets figure a utility tractor at $30,000. A used 40 to 75 hp tractor with a loader, 10 to 20 years old, runs from about $20,000 to $45,000 at dealers and auctions.

est_trailer.name: Estimate: stock trailer
est_trailer.basis: No published price report. A used 16 ft bumper-pull runs about $8,000, a new one $12,000 to $16,000, a gooseneck $18,000 to $25,000 at dealers.

est_truck.name: Estimate: used 3/4-ton truck
est_truck.basis: Edmunds put the average 3-year-old used vehicle at $30,699 in late 2025. Three-quarter-ton trucks hold value and run higher; an older one with miles runs lower.

est_horse.name: Estimate: using horse
est_horse.basis: No published average. Sound, broke using horses commonly sell from $2,500 to $10,000 at ranch horse sales.

est_pullet.name: Estimate: started pullets
est_pullet.basis: Chicks run $6 (Maryland Extension, 2026). Started pullets near laying age cost more because someone fed them for four months.

est_egg_value.name: Estimate: store value of a dozen eggs
est_egg_value.basis: Maryland Extension figures the cost to raise a dozen at $3.37. Store eggs ran $3 to $6 a dozen in 2025.

est_surprises.name: Estimate: cushion for surprises
est_surprises.basis: 5% to 15% on top of everything. Rock in the trench, a bad culvert, a second load of gravel.

est_ag_share.name: Estimate: ag valuation share
est_ag_share.basis: Where land qualifies for agricultural use valuation, it is taxed on a fraction of market value, commonly a tenth to a quarter. Varies by state and county; ask the appraisal district.

nass_rent_2025.name: USDA NASS Quick Stats, cash rent for pastureland by state, 2025
nass_rent_2025.basis: Pasture cash rent per acre, 2025: US $15.50, Texas $7.70, Oklahoma $18, Arkansas $22, Tennessee $26, Kentucky $35, Missouri $38.50. State averages lean on big native-range leases; improved pasture near town rents higher.

isu_rent_2026.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker C2-10, Cash Rental Rates for Iowa 2026 Survey
isu_rent_2026.basis: Pasture $27 per animal unit month. Improved pasture $102 an acre, poor pasture $63 an acre, statewide, 1,450 responses.

unl_realestate_2026.name: University of Nebraska, Nebraska Farm Real Estate Market Highlights 2025-2026, Table 11
unl_realestate_2026.basis: Pasture rent per cow-calf pair per month, 2026, by district: $56.45 to $82.10. Stocker calf $32 to $51 a month. The monthly rate is traditionally multiplied by a five-month season.

osu_cr216_2021.name: Oklahoma State University Extension CR-216, Oklahoma Pasture Rental Rates 2020-21
osu_cr216_2021.basis: Native pasture $15.42 an acre, bermudagrass $20.22. Grazing season 9.1 months. 9.4 acres per cow on native range. Of 623 leases, the livestock owner paid for mineral in 98%, fence labor in 85%, fence materials in 73%, water in 75%.

ncfmec03_2011.name: North Central Farm Management Extension Committee, NCFMEC-03, Pasture Rental Arrangements for Your Farm
ncfmec03_2011.basis: Sample lease assigns fence repair, water, mineral, checking cattle, vet calls and fly control to landlord or tenant by checkbox. Yearling example $25 a month for a four-month season.

ncfmec06_2013.name: North Central Farm Management Extension Committee, NCFMEC-06, Beef Cow Rental Arrangements for Your Farm
ncfmec06_2013.basis: Worked example: the operator who supplies grass, hay, labor and management contributes 65.9% of the cost and takes 65.9% of the calf money; the cow owner 34.1%. The owner keeps all cull cow sales. Labor 5.65 hours per cow per year. Leased bulls run $700 or more a season.

isu_c2_33_2011.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker C2-33, Beef Cow Joint Agreements
isu_c2_33_2011.basis: When the owner supplies the cows and the pasture, calf income splits 40% owner, 60% operator. A labor-only party earns 20% to 25% of the calf crop.

unl_custom_2025.name: University of Nebraska, Custom Service Rates Related to Livestock Production in Nebraska 2025
unl_custom_2025.basis: Care for cow-calf pairs on summer pasture, not counting pasture rent or feed: $1.00 per head per day. Wintering cows $1.56 a day, range $0.83 to $2.40.

ksu_bluestem_2025.name: Kansas State University and Kansas Department of Agriculture, Bluestem Pasture Release 2025
ksu_bluestem_2025.basis: A 1,250 lb cow-calf pair for the full summer: $276.25 with care, $210.84 without, so care is worth about $65 a pair a season. 600 lb stocker $133.75 with care. 8.1 acres per pair.

tamu_stocker_2025.name: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension, 2025 stocker budgets, District 8 native pasture and District 11 Coastal Bend
tamu_stocker_2025.basis: District 8: buy a 400 lb calf at $360 a cwt ($1,440), sell at 750 lb and $255, grazing 5 acres at $14, labor $15.83, returns to management $107.63 a head. District 11: buy 500 lb at $310 ($1,550), 160 days grazing, returns $10.99 a head.

ams_grassfed_2026.name: USDA AMS, National Grass Fed Beef Report, 2026 Quarter 3
ams_grassfed_2026.basis: Direct sales by hanging weight, processing not included: whole $4.00 to $7.90 (average $5.90), half average $5.76, quarter $6.23. Processing paid by the customer: $0.94 a pound hanging plus a $125 slaughter fee. 84 producers.

msu_freezer_2026.name: Michigan State University Extension, How to price freezer beef
msu_freezer_2026.basis: Dressing percentage: beef-type cattle 62% to 64%, grass-fed steers 50% to 60%. Example 1,400 lb steer, 882 lb carcass, $3.80 a pound hanging, breakeven $3.73.

uaex_fsa3143_2021.name: University of Arkansas Extension FSA3143, Raising Calves for Slaughter
uaex_fsa3143_2021.basis: Forage-finished calves are often slaughtered near 1,000 lb live. Growing a 500 lb calf to 1,000 lb on forage takes about 367 days at 1.5 lb a day. Dressing 58% to 66%.

isu_b1_21_2026.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker B1-21, Livestock Enterprise Budgets for Iowa 2026
isu_b1_21_2026.basis: A 550 lb steer calf valued at $4.92 a pound, $2,706. Finishing it to 1,350 lb takes nine months, 69 bushels of corn, total cost $3,581.

sare_grassfed_2026.name: SARE, Enterprise Budgets for Diversified Farms, Case Study 3, Bottom Line Profitability for Grassfed Steers
sare_grassfed_2026.basis: Steers finished at about 24 months. Net return selling locker beef by the half: minus $358 a head; selling boxed cuts: plus $154 a head, with a $30,000 cold storage room.

mu_g204_2026.name: University of Missouri Extension G204, Evaluating Direct-to-Consumer Marketing Opportunities for Local Beef
mu_g204_2026.basis: Processing into retail cuts $847 an animal. Half beef priced at $2.78 a pound live, quarter $2.93, live sale $2.38.

nebguide_g2364_2024.name: University of Nebraska NebGuide G2364, Development of a Direct Marketing Beef Program: Custom vs. Inspected
nebguide_g2364_2024.basis: Custom-exempt beef must be sold as a live animal before slaughter and is marked not for sale; retail cuts need a USDA-inspected plant and freezers. Small processors book 6 to 24 months out.

fsa_rates_2026.name: USDA Farm Service Agency, Current FSA Loan Interest Rates
fsa_rates_2026.basis: Farm operating, direct and microloan: 5.625%. Farm ownership direct: 6.25%. Down payment loan: 2.25%.

fsa_chart_2025.name: USDA Farm Service Agency, Farm Loan Information Chart
fsa_chart_2025.basis: Direct operating loan up to $400,000, 1 to 7 years, for livestock and equipment. Operating microloan up to $50,000, rate capped at 5% for beginning and veteran farmers. Farm ownership up to $600,000 over 40 years. A beginning farmer is anyone under ten years in.

isu_custom_2026.name: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker A3-10, 2026 Iowa Farm Custom Rate Survey
isu_custom_2026.basis: Large round bales $13.15 each without wrap, $15.75 with. Mowing $15.45 an acre, raking $9.90. Mowing pasture $27.05 an acre, chopping brush $105.55. Hauling cattle by semi $4.70 a loaded mile. Fence building labor $42.70 an hour.

unl_custom_2026.name: University of Nebraska, 2026 Nebraska Agricultural Custom Rates Report
unl_custom_2026.basis: Baling large round bales with net wrap $17.88 a bale. Building four-strand barbed wire fence, labor only, $1.60 a foot. Mowing pasture $4.60 an acre.

nass_cropvalues_2026.name: USDA NASS, Crop Values 2025 Summary
nass_cropvalues_2026.basis: All other hay, 2025 marketing year, dollars a ton: US $138, Texas $136, Oklahoma $161, Missouri $125.

hud_fmr_2026.name: HUD, FY 2026 Fair Market Rents, Texas nonmetropolitan counties
hud_fmr_2026.basis: Fannin County, TX: 2 bedroom $985, 3 bedroom $1,370, 4 bedroom $1,652 a month. Look up any county at huduser.gov.

est_labor_small.name: Estimate: hours per cow for a small herd
est_labor_small.basis: Texas A&M budgets 3.72 hours a cow a year on a 200-cow ranch; the NCFMEC cow-lease worksheet uses 5.65. A man with 20 cows and no help spends more per cow; the high figure allows for that.

est_calf_crop.name: Estimate: calf crop and share of cow income from calves
est_calf_crop.basis: The Texas A&M 2025 budget sells 0.655 calves per cow after keeping replacement heifers and culls 12% of cows, which implies about 85 calves weaned per 100 cows. Cull cows are about 13% of a cow's yearly income in that budget.

est_finish_carry.name: Estimate: carrying a weaned calf a year to grass finish
est_finish_carry.basis: No published budget for grass-finishing a calf on leased pasture. Half the keep-a-cow line covers hay, mineral and vet; grazing is added at the lease rate for 0.7 of a cow's acres.

est_handling.name: Estimate: handling setup on leased grass
est_handling.basis: Twenty 12 ft panels at about $140 each (Priefert economy panel, retail), a used or economy squeeze chute ($3,000 to $5,800 at farm stores), a stock tank and mineral feeders. No manufacturer price list is published.

est_calf_value_high.name: Estimate: top of the weaned calf range
est_calf_value_high.basis: Low is the Texas A&M January 2025 budget (525 lb steer at $295 a cwt, $1,549). Typical is Iowa State June 2026 (550 lb at $4.92, $2,706). High allows a bit over the 2026 price.

est_share_high.name: Estimate: top of the operator share
est_share_high.basis: Published splits run 60% (owner also supplies grass) to 65.9% (operator supplies grass). An operator who also supplies the bull and hauls to market can argue for 70%.
